To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have optimized the production of NKp30ex protein in E. coli and have shown that it can be obtained in high purity and homogeneity in a single step, and that it is suitable for NMR studies at temperatures up to 40 degrees C.

the production of soluble NKp30ex protein is possible using low cost M9 minimal media with low concentrations of (13)C-d- or (15)N-d-glucose and that the protein is stable for long periods at 4°C and at room temperature.
we have developed a protocol for production of soluble NKp30ex protein in a form suitable for structural studies using high-resolution NMR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, highly efficient and cost-effective production protocol for NKp30ex.
the development of a new and efficient production protocol for the extracellular domain of NKp30.
the development of a protocol for production of isotopically enriched NKp30ex for structural studies using advanced NMR techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the production protocol presented here is a very good and robust tool for producing isotopically labeled human NKp30ex protein for advanced NMR structural studies.
our optimized protocol for producing isotopically enriched NKp30ex is very efficient and reliable.
our optimized procedure allows to produce soluble NKp30 in a very efficient way, which is crucial for the success of structural studies using NHR spectroscopy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the production of NKp30ex in E. coli is now a reliable and routine process that allows to produce the protein in a highly pure, stable, monomeric and homogeneous form in sufficient amounts for structural and functional studies using NMR spectroscopy.
the optimized production of NKp30ex on M9 medium is a simple and reliable protocol to produce sufficient amounts of this protein for structural studies.
we report a very efficient protocol to produce soluble monomeric proteins in a homogenous state in high yields.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a codon optimization of the gene encoding for the protein to be produced can be very helpful in improving the production yield.
the production of soluble proteins in M9 media is a viable option even for proteins with low expression levels.
it is possible to obtain milligram quantities of soluble monomeric proteins from E. coli using a codon- optimized gene fragment and minimal media containing (15)-labeled amino acids.
